subject: [hw] V41 -> IP/lead: FIRST-ENCODE BLOCKER in vcodecd read_sequence_header -- header buffer is not in the n2vc_dma registry (4-line fix, new test)
body:
Found while checking the daemon against my API before the phone run. This fails on the phone at N2VCD_OPEN/start, before any frame:

  daemon/vcodecd.c read_sequence_header() (lines 515-539):
      int r = hw->dma_alloc(hw->ctx, bytes, 0, &handle, &pa);   // handle NOT in n2vc_dma
      ...
      r = n2ap_venc_encode(enc, 0, handle, N2AP_ENC_SEQ_HDR, &res);

  n2ap_venc_encode() -> n2ap_venc_encode_fd() resolves the bitstream handle with
  n2vc_dma_lookup_handle(); a handle that only went through hw->dma_alloc() is not in that
  registry, so it returns -EINVAL before sending AP_IPIMSG_ENC_ENCODE. Result: every session
  fails at "sequence-header job failed: -22", then N2VCD_E_ARGS. It does not show in the daemon
  tests because daemon/test/fake_vhost.c returns -ENOENT from n2vc_dma_lookup_handle and
  -ENOSYS from n2vc_dma_guest_register ("the fake AP model does not need PAs").

[V] Proven in the V41 suite (new test, this tree): allocate exactly as vcodecd does, call
n2ap_venc_encode(seq hdr) -> -EINVAL and n_encode==0 (no message); then
n2vc_dma_guest_register(hw, NULL, handle, pa, bytes, NULL) -> 0 and the same call -> 0 with
bytes=29, enc_bsaddr==pa, enc_bsva==0x80000000|handle.

  bash gpu/hwcodec/ap/test_v41/run_tests.sh
  -> N2TEST V41 PASS 667/667   (628 x ASan+UBSan/-O2/TSan + 39 real n2vcu; was 651)

Exact fix in your file (read_sequence_header; n2ap_venc.h already declares both calls):

      int r = hw->dma_alloc(hw->ctx, bytes, 0, &handle, &pa);
      if (r != 0) { return r; }
 +    /* V41 resolves the bitstream handle in n2vc_dma; hw->dma_alloc() does not register it. */
 +    r = n2vc_dma_guest_register(hw, NULL, handle, pa, bytes, NULL);
 +    if (r == -EEXIST) { (void)n2vc_dma_guest_forget(hw, handle);
 +                        r = n2vc_dma_guest_register(hw, NULL, handle, pa, bytes, NULL); }
 +    if (r != 0 && r != -ENOSYS) { (void)hw->dma_free(hw->ctx, handle); return r; }
      ...
      (void)hw->dma_free(hw->ctx, handle);
 +    (void)n2vc_dma_guest_forget(hw, handle);
      return r;

The -ENOSYS tolerance keeps daemon/test/fake_vhost.c working unchanged (its stand-in registry
refuses); the real n2vc_dma.c never returns -ENOSYS, so product behaviour is unchanged except
that the handle now resolves. n2vc_dma_guest_forget() must be called BEFORE dma_free() or a
later reused handle can still match a stale pa.

Same pattern applies to any other buffer the daemon allocates itself and hands to
n2ap_venc_encode() (only this one today). No phone, nothing published; the tree files are
untouched by me (only ap/test_v41/t_v41.c gained the regression test).
